title: Acceleration of two connected blocks
canonical_question: How do you calculate the acceleration of two connected blocks pulled by one force?
summary: When two blocks are joined by a rope and pulled, the simplest first step is to treat them as a single mass equal to their total.
To get the rope tension, apply F = ma to just one block using the shared acceleration.

reuse.rationale: Authored fixture node for the E05 registry.

sections.heading: Treat them as one system
sections.body_md: When two blocks are joined by a rope and pulled, the simplest first step is to treat them as a single mass equal to their total. The applied force divided by the total mass gives the shared acceleration. Both blocks accelerate together at that rate.

sections.heading: Finding the internal tension
sections.body_md: To get the rope tension, apply F = ma to just one block using the shared acceleration. The tension is whatever force gives that block its share of the acceleration. Splitting the system this way solves both unknowns.

key_points: Total force over total mass gives the acceleration.
Apply F = ma to one block for the tension.
core.bridge_to_parent: It extends the objective’s method to a two-body system.
